phases.objective: Execute one mounted Tenant storage operation through Context Kernel authority, one canonical repository instance, immutable-plan consumption, prepared/result/readback journaling, reconciliation, and Tenant-safe readback while preserving the no-provider and no-Production safety boundary.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The same canonical repository records the exact operation completion, consumed immutable plan, append-only approvals, prepared/result/readback journal phases, one reconciliation result, and Tenant-safe response bindings for the same operation, run, plan, outcome, and result digest.
steps: Resolve Context Kernel identity for the exact Tenant, workspace, user, and request.
Resolve effective resource authority and reject request-side authority injection or cross-Tenant access before mutation.

Execute through the mounted Tenant route using one canonical repository instance, an expected-SHA-bound immutable plan, append-only approval evidence, one-shot enablement, and the fixed synthetic executor.

Re-read the exact operation from the same repository and prove completed state, unchanged immutable plan bindings, unchanged append-only approval digests, prepared/result/readback journal phases, and one reconciliation result.

Bind the Tenant-safe response to the same operation, run, plan, outcome, and result digest while provider dispatch, live mutation, SQL Apply, deployment, Production readiness, and secrets remain disabled.
assertions: The mounted request and post-request readback use the same repository object and operation ID.
The immutable plan bindings remain unchanged while its single-use consumed state advances.
Approval record digests remain append-only and unchanged.
Prepared, result, and readback journal records persist for the same operation, run, and plan.
Exactly one reconciliation result matches the Tenant-safe response outcome and result digest.
The Tenant-safe response is bound to the same operation, run, plan, outcome, and result digest.
Cross-Tenant requests, request-side authority injection, and expected-SHA drift fail before mutation.
Provider dispatch, live mutation, SQL Apply, deployment, Production readiness, and secrets remain false.

phases.objective: Preserve the MVP journey while adding cancellation, lease release, approval revocation, bounded retries, and operator-visible state transitions.
Prove fault injection, worker restart recovery, unknown-outcome reconciliation, checkpoint restoration, and inode-exhaustion reserve release.
Run the same journey against one allowlisted non-production Tenant root, then a governed shared/platform target with impact-set approvals.
Enable read-only Production preflight first, then require exact Production SHA and runtime readback before any separately governed mutation capability.

declared_overlaps.reason: Recovery verification evidence must be consumed fail-closed by the canonical Durable execution authorization bundle.

The synthetic executor must preserve and validate the same hardened attestation, recovery, evidence-integrity, and release-provenance readbacks introduced at the Recovery and Durable integration boundary.
The contracts workstream owns the Spec package broadly while this bounded readback owns only final Work Map governance bindings and T006 evidence.
